name: hono-middleware-composition-policies
instr:
Hono's `except` folds its conditions with the synchronous `Array.prototype.some`, so an `async` condition returns a truthy Promise and the guarded middleware is always skipped — a fail-open bypass. Make `except` await its conditions, so that async and sync conditions behave identically across `some`, `every` and `except`, and build a policy layer on that awaiting evaluator.

Publish a new subpath `hono/policy`, rooted at `src/policy/`, entry module `src/policy/index.ts`, added to `package.json` `exports` as `{"types": "./dist/types/policy/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/policy/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/policy/index.js"}` and to `jsr.json` `exports` as `"./policy": "./src/policy/index.ts"`. Add exactly that one entry to each manifest and no others. Every type, function and error class named below is exported from that entry.

Types: `PolicyOutcome` = `'allow' | 'deny' | 'skip' | 'error'`; `PolicyDecisionInit` = `{ allow: boolean; reason?: string }`; `PolicyCondition<E extends Env = any>` = `(c: Context<E>) => boolean | PolicyDecisionInit | Promise<boolean | PolicyDecisionInit>`; `PolicyDecision` `{ policy, outcome, reason, frameId, sequence }`; `PolicyFrame` `{ id, parentId, depth, index }`; `Policy<E extends Env = any>` = `MiddlewareHandler<E> & { readonly policyName: string }`, accepted by `createMiddleware` and by handler registration.
